heading: INT. WIRELESS ROOM - S.S. CALYPSO - NIGHT, 1923

units.text: INT. WIRELESS ROOM - S.S. CALYPSO - NIGHT, 1923
A cramped brass-and-mahogany cabin lit by a green-shaded lamp.
The telegraph key chatters.
Beyond the porthole, a black sea.
LADY PHILIPPA ASHGROVE, fifties, in a fur-collared evening gown, waits with gloved hands folded.
At the desk, young AMBROSE TILLERY, the wireless operator, copies a message with a pencil.
Behind her, MR. CORNELIUS BLY, sixty, a banker with a white moustache, stands very still.
In the corner sits MADAME ZORKA DRAGOMIR, a fortune-teller with a velvet shawl, humming softly.
That's the last of it, my lady. "Meet at Southampton. Say nothing."
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: Thank you, Ambrose. Cornelius, you may relax.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: I am perfectly relaxed.
units.name: BLY

units.text: Of course you are.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: The sea is very calm tonight.
units.name: ZORKA

units.text: The door opens.
INSPECTOR HALVARD STROM, forties, in a damp greatcoat and bowler, steps inside, a pair of handcuffs dangling from one hand.
Mr. Cornelius Bly. I have a warrant from Scotland Yard.
units.name: STROM

units.text: Bly turns.
Philippa's gloved hands do not move.
Madame Zorka stops humming.
I did say nothing.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: You said nothing was the plan.
units.name: BLY

units.text: Oh, dear.
units.name: AMBROSE
